about: One record per public operation. Generated by alwan_dev/tools/gen_capability_manifest.py from alwan.h, core/, api/, map/, experimental/ and docs/backend_matrix.csv; do not edit by hand.

legend.id: stable capability identifier, independent of the C spelling of precision and buffer form
legend.status: stable: part of the 3.x API; experimental: under src/alwan/experimental, may change and is not deterministic
legend.scope: pointwise: each output pixel depends on its input pixel and the parameters only (fusable); image: needs the whole image or a statistic of it; other: neither (fits, loaders, queries)
legend.allocates: a static scan of the implementation and everything it calls: yes means it may allocate; map functions never allocate except runtime-data first touch (allocates_runtime_data, only with ALWAN_EMBED_DATA=0)
legend.in_place: map functions accept out == in when both have the same format and stride; any other overlap is undefined
legend.core: the pure per-pixel evaluation: C names per precision, and the single-precision GPU name (HLSL, GLSL, Halide, and the CUDA / OpenCL float build). null: no core, the operation is C only
legend.backends: C: tested by the suites. SIMD: simd_map (vector kernels) or scalar_loop. HLSL: compiled_ci (dxc and fxc in CI), run_bitexact / run_tolerance (run on D3D12 WARP and compared), compiled_not_gated, none. GLSL: lint_only (never compiled). Halide: none (never built). OpenCL / CUDA: compiled_manual (compiled by hand), run_bitexact_det_and_tolerance_fast (this kernel run and compared with C: 0 ULP in the deterministic build, a tolerance in the fast build). A compiled core is not a verified one: only the run_* states were compared with C.
legend.precision: C: f32 and f64 where both symbols exist. GPU: single precision only; CUDA also f64; OpenCL fp64 never tested.
legend.determinism: see docs/determinism.md and docs/host-integration.md: bitwise only for the deterministic C build across the CI runners, and for the GPU kernels marked run_bitexact_*; everything else is tolerance

core: alwan_xyz_to_lab_{T}_v and the other colorspace / oklab / convenience cores
gaps: alwan_rgb_convert_{T} adapts only with a ctx, alwan_image_convert always (see migration manifest)
the method-to-cone-matrix choice is C only: pass the matrix from alwan_cat_matrix to the shader
CIE 1994, vK20 and Li 2025 recompute the adaptation per pixel and have no map

core: alwan_<tf>_oetf_{T} / alwan_<tf>_eotf_{T} (C), alwan_<tf>_oetf / _eotf (GPU); table in transfer_functions
gaps: no switch-on-enum core: a generator picks the core by name from transfer_functions
methods ADAPTIVE_CUSP to RAYTRACE are C only (alwan_gamut_map_advanced)
the spatial gamut maps are image operations, not pointwise

core: a plain exposure is rgb * exp2(EV): no core needed
alwan_view_core.inc curves (reinhard, hable, uchimura, lottes, khronos_pbr_neutral, ...)
gaps: the complete view transforms (clamps, decodes, constants) are static C in api/alwan_view_impl.inc
ACES 1.x and 2.0 output transforms compose their cores inside the C map; the ACES 2.0 parameter init is static C
alwan_tonemap_global needs an image reduction first (global)
Hellwig 2022 has no parameter split (recomputes D and FL per pixel) and no map
SPD to XYZ is a dot product with the prepared weights: write it in the kernel
the four spectral upsamplers are C only

core: through ALWAN_TABLE_READ(i), which the shader binds to its buffer
gaps: alwan_lut1d/2d/3d_sample_*_v take pointers and are compiled out on HLSL and GLSL: shaders call the named table readers
